If you don't want your child to hide from you, stop doing these. 🐢

Kids don't start out hiding. Ezra is seven, and little by little, he pulls on a shell:
✅ Don't punish the truth. "Go to your room!" before you've even dealt with it.
✅ Don't lecture.
✅ Don't yell when he tells you something hard. "WHAT?!"
✅ Don't call him "too sensitive." It hurts.
✅ Don't brush off his problems. What's small to you is huge to him.
✅ Don't make mistakes scary. "I made a mistake…"
✅ Don't make honesty unsafe.

What does fear teach? In a study comparing a harsh, punishing school with a gentler one, children from the punishing school lied more, and they lied well (Talwar & Lee, Child Development, 2011). 😔

So one night, Mom sits on his bed and says: "I will never stop loving you. You can tell me anything." ❤️

That's what Jesus did for us, so we'd never have to hide. "Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need." Hebrews 4:16 (ESV) 🙏

At fifteen, Ezra walks straight to his mom with the hard stuff. ❤️ Be the one they run to, not the one they hide from. Especially when they're hiding worries inside.
